The sufficient condition, and the new necessary condition, associated with the excess function, as well as the expression for the variation as <math>\int\text{E}ds</math>, are due to Weierstrass. In applications to special problems it is generally permissible to identify <math>\text{A}'</math> with <math>\text{A}</math>, and to regard <math>\text{QP}</math> as straight. The direction of <math>\text{QP}</math> must be such that the integral of <math>\text{F}</math> taken along it is finite and real. We shall describe such directions as ''admissible.'' In the statement of the sufficient condition, and the new necessary condition, it is of course understood that the direction specified by <math>\psi</math> is admissible. {{block center|<math>\text{E}(x,\ y,\ \tan\phi,\ \tan\psi)</math>}}

{{block center|<math>=\cos\psi\left\{\text{F}(x,y,\ \tan\psi)-\text{F}(x,y,p)-(\tan\psi-p)\frac{\partial\text{F}}{\partial p}\right\}_{p=\tan\phi}.</math>}}
